headline: Trump posts 'Complete and Total Endorsement' of Netanyahu for Israel's Oct 27 Knesset election'
dek: Trump endorsed Netanyahu for the Oct 27 election, praised him as a 'Great Warrior Prime Minister' and partner against Iran, claimed Iran was 'systematically destroyed, both Militarily and Financially', and warned that with anyone other than Netanyahu, the US would have to 'finish the job' itself —…
sources: Donald Trump's Truth Social post (Sunday); Netanyahu replied on X ('Together we will complete the mission') and released an election video framing the vote as 'ensuring Israel's survival' and 'fateful: right - or Palesti
fault_line: Foreign endorsement vs interference: should a US president pick the winner of another democracy's election? And 'finish the job' on Iran — partnership or escalation?

sections.what_happened: Trump endorsed Netanyahu for the Oct 27 election, praised him as a 'Great Warrior Prime Minister' and partner against Iran, claimed Iran was 'systematically destroyed, both Militarily and Financially', and warned that with anyone other than Netanyahu, the US would have to 'finish the job' itself — which he is 'not inclined to do'. Election is Israel's first national vote since the Oct 7 2023 Hamas attack; race tight (Oct 14-15 polls: opposition Jewish-led bloc 54 vs Netanyahu bloc 49 per Zman Yisrael; Maariv 51-51), challenger ex-army chief Gadi Eisenkot (Yashar) and Naftali Bennett (B'Yachad).
sections.what_verified: Reuters wire + Haaretz + Times of Israel liveblog + WION + TOI + Economic Times all report the same post language; Netanyahu's X reply verified in Vanguard/WION. Quotes consistent across outlets.
sections.what_disputed: Counterpoint: Trump said in August he would stay out of Israeli elections ('I think it's most appropriate for me to stay out'); challengers Eisenkot/Bennett positioned as viable alternatives; polls show no clear Netanyahu majority. Trump's 'systematically destroyed' Iran claim is HIS claim — no independent verification of that assessment; treat as primary-source claim, not fact.
sections.why_matters: From the side of truth: Washington openly stakes US Iran policy on keeping Netanyahu in power — 9 days before Israelis vote. Tehran, which has watched Israel expand the Gaza war into Lebanon and Iran, reads this as a declared escalation commitment, not an election courtesy. Verified facts only; Trump's Iran claims flagged as his claims.
sections.context: Background: US/Israel — NEW in-window: Trump posts 'Complete and Total Endorsement' of Netanyahu for Israel's Oct 27 Knesset election; warns wrong leader means 'America will have to do this work ourselves' on Iran; 'we will soon finish the job'
